bib.title: The Upper Confidence Bound Algorithm: Bernoulli Noise (Chapter 10 of Bandit Algorithms)
bib.venue: Bandit Algorithms, Cambridge University Press (book chapter 10)

question: How can the UCB index be tightened for Bernoulli rewards by using Chernoff/relative-entropy confidence bounds instead of subgaussian ones?
hypothesis: Because Bernoulli variance depends on the mean, confidence intervals can shrink near 0 or 1, so a KL-based index should have regret never worse than UCB and better when means are near 0 or 1.
contributions: Chernoff bound and its inversion into KL confidence bounds U(a), L(a) (Lemma 10.3, Corollary 10.4)
KL-UCB algorithm (Algorithm 8) with finite-time and asymptotic regret bound (Theorem 10.6)
Extensions to [0,1]-supported rewards and exponential families in notes and exercises

results.claim: Finite-time regret bound of KL-UCB for Bernoulli bandits (Theorem 10.6).
results.setup: Bernoulli bandit, k arms, mean vector mu in [0,1]^k, horizon n, reward X_t ~ B(mu_{A_t}); KL-UCB (Algorithm 8) with f(t)=1+t log^2(t)
results.note: Formula (verbatim from text, symbols): R_n <= sum_{i:Delta_i>0} inf_{eps1,eps2>0, eps1+eps2 in (0,Delta_i)} Delta_i ( log f(n) / d(mu_i+eps1, mu*-eps2) + 1/(2 eps1^2) + 2/eps2^2 ). Proof gives E[T_i(n)] <= 2/eps2^2 + log f(n)/d(mu_i+eps1,mu*-eps2) + 1/(2 eps1^2).

results.claim: Asymptotic regret of KL-UCB: limsup R_n/log n <= sum Delta_i / d(mu_i, mu*).
results.setup: Bernoulli bandit, k arms, mean vector mu in [0,1]^k, horizon n, reward X_t ~ B(mu_{A_t}); KL-UCB (Algorithm 8) with f(t)=1+t log^2(t); n to infinity
results.note: limsup R_n/log(n) <= sum_{i:Delta_i>0} Delta_i/d(mu_i,mu*). Asymptotic proof left as Exercise 10.2 (choose eps1,eps2 decreasing slowly with n).

results.claim: UCB (Ch. 8) with subgaussian constant sigma=1/2 has asymptotic regret sum 1/(2 Delta_i); KL-UCB is never worse because d(mu_i,mu*) >= 2 Delta_i^2 (Pinsker).
results.setup: Bernoulli bandit; comparison of asymptotic constants
results.quote: which means that the asymptotic regret of KL-UCB is never worse than that of UCB

results.claim: Taylor expansion: d(mu_i,mu*) = Delta_i^2/(2 mu_i(1-mu_i)) + o(Delta_i^2), so KL-UCB regret is approx sum 2 mu_i(1-mu_i)/Delta_i; improves on UCB when mu_i near 0 or 1.
results.setup: small gaps (mu_i close to mu*), asymptotic regime
results.quote: indicating that the regret of KL-UCB is approximately

results.claim: Pinsker's inequality for Bernoulli relative entropy: d(p,q) >= 2(p-q)^2.
Chernoff bound: P(mu_hat >= mu+eps) <= exp(-n d(mu+eps, mu)) for eps in [0,1-mu]; symmetric lower tail.
Inverting the Chernoff bound: with U(a)=max{u in [0,1]: d(mu_hat,u)<=a}, P(mu >= U(a)) <= exp(-na); setting a=log(1/delta)/n gives upper/lower confidence bounds.
Worked example: mu_hat=3/4, n=10, 90 per cent confidence gives a approx 0.23; interval is highly asymmetric and Hoeffding's upper bound is vacuous.
results.setup: mu_hat = 3/4, n = 10, confidence 90 per cent, a = log(1/delta)/n

results.claim: Hoeffding interval width stays at sqrt(log(1/delta)/(2n)) as mu_hat approaches 1, whereas the KL interval width U(a)-mu_hat goes to 0.
results.setup: mu_hat to 1, fixed n and delta
results.quote: the width of the interval U(a) −ˆµ approaches zero

results.claim: Lemma 10.7: expected time for the optimal arm's index to reach mu - eps is at most 2/eps^2.
Lemma 10.8: E[kappa] <= inf over eps in (0,Delta) of a/d(mu+eps, mu+Delta) + 1/(2 eps^2).
Chernoff bound and KL-UCB results extend to any rewards supported in [0,1] (via MGF bound of Garivier and Cappe 2011, Lemma 9), with the same limsup bound.
The [0,1]-supported bound is not tight: an algorithm exists with limsup R_n/log n = sum Delta_i/d_i where d_i = inf{D(P_i,P): mu(P)>mu*, Supp(P) in [0,1]} >= d(mu_i,mu*).
results.quote: The quantity di is never smaller than d(µi, µ∗).

results.claim: Asymptotics for Bernoulli bandits understood since Lai and Robbins 1985; earliest version of KL-UCB due to Lai 1987; finite-time analysis by Garivier and Cappe 2011 and Maillard et al. 2011.
results.quote: asymptotics have been well understood since the article by Lai and Robbins [1985]

results.claim: For canonical exponential families, E[T_i(n)] approx log(n)/d_{i,inf} + 1/d_{i,min}; the second term is negligible asymptotically but may dominate for all reasonable n.
results.quote: it may be the dominant term for all reasonable n

results.claim: CLT does not justify treating the Bernoulli bandit as a Gaussian bandit with matched variance, because confidence levels must shrink with n and the CLT says nothing about tails below O(n^-1/2).
results.quote: But the central limit theorem does not provide information about the tails

limits: Chapter has no experiments; simulation is left as Exercise 10.6 (n=10000, k=2, mu1=1/2 and mu2=1/2+Delta; repeat with mu1=1/10 and 9/10), so no regret numbers are reported.
The asymptotic claim of Theorem 10.6 is left as Exercise 10.2.

The Lai-Robbins lower bound is not stated in this chapter; only cited (Sec 10.4) and the constant sum Delta_i/d(mu_i,mu*) matches its form for Bernoulli arms. Optimality for [0,1]-supported rewards needs a different algorithm (Honda and Takemura 2010; DMED, IMED).
Exponential family extension only as exercises 10.4, 10.5 (Ch. 34).
Extraction lost section headings; algorithm box rendered as text (index formula intact).
practices: For Bernoulli rewards (e.g. click-through), use KL-UCB instead of subgaussian UCB because the index tightens near 0 or 1 (intro, Sec 10.2).
Compute the KL index by Newton's method since d has no closed-form inverse and is convex in its second argument (after Cor 10.4).
Expect KL-UCB to help most where arm means are near 0 or 1 (Eq 10.5).
The finite-time lower-order term 1/d_{i,min} may dominate for realistic n (Exercise 10.4 comment).
